candidates.name: Puerto Rican Pernil Pork Bowls with Rice and Beans
candidates.why: Oven-roasted marinated pork shoulder, the cheapest pork cut on the board, shredded over rice and beans. Source states 324 cal / 52g protein per serving for the meat alone (12 servings from a 6 lb shoulder); with rice and beans a full dinner portion lands 600+ cal and comfortably 35g+ protein. Roast-and-shred is ideal weigh-and-divide batch food. Catalog has Cuban mojo pork but no Puerto Rican pernil.

candidates.name: Cochinita Pibil Pork Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Slow cooker achiote-citrus pork; achiote-paste is already a tracked board commodity, so the signature ingredient maps cleanly. Source states 214 cal / 23.5g protein per meat serving over 12 servings; over rice with black beans a dinner portion is 550-600 cal and 30g+ protein. Distinct from the live carnitas/al pastor/salsa verde pork entries (achiote + sour orange, not chile or pineapple).

candidates.name: Brazilian Feijoada Pork and Black Bean Stew Bowls
unmapped_flags: smoked ham hock (no board id; deli-ham or kielbasa substitutes)
candidates.why: National dish of Brazil, slow cooker, black beans plus pork shoulder and bacon over rice. Beans carry the calories and pork carries the protein, so it holds 500+ cal and 30g+ at real portions. Confidence note: source page publishes no nutrition panel, so the calorie/protein figures here are my estimate from the ingredient list, not verified from the page. Live catalog has Brazilian-style pork ribs but no feijoada.

candidates.name: Asado de Puerco (Mexican Red Chile Pork Stew) Bowls
unmapped_flags: dried guajillo/ancho chiles (board tracks chili-powder, not whole dried chiles)
candidates.why: Pork simmered in red chile colorado sauce; source states 293 cal / 26g protein per serving over 10 servings for the stew, so plated over rice and beans it clears 550+ cal and 30g protein. Distinct from the live green chili and salsa verde pork bowls (red chile, not green). Braise scales linearly to 14 servings.

candidates.name: Pozole Rojo (Red Pork and Hominy Stew) Bowls
unmapped_flags: dried guajillo/ancho/arbol chiles (board tracks chili-powder only)
candidates.why: Hominy is already a board commodity. Source states 194 cal / 16g protein per serving at 10 servings, which is thin, so this needs a heavier meat ratio and a rice or tortilla side to reach dinner size. Confidence note: est_cal here assumes we raise pork per serving and serve it as a full bowl, not the source's soup portion. The live catalog has Posole Verde; red pozole with dried chiles is the distinct classic version.

candidates.name: Mexican Adobada Pork Shoulder Bowls
unmapped_flags: dried guajillo/ancho chiles
piloncillo (brown-sugar substitutes and is on the board)
candidates.why: Oven-braised chile-adobo pork butt, 4 hours covered, shredded for bowls. Confidence note: no nutrition panel on the source page, so est_cal is my estimate from ingredients. Adjacent to the live al pastor entry but genuinely different (vinegar-chile adobo, no pineapple/achiote spit style) - flag for the dedup stage to adjudicate.

candidates.name: New Mexico Carne Adovada Pork Bowls
unmapped_flags: dried New Mexico/ancho/guajillo chiles (board tracks chili-powder only)
candidates.why: Source verified at 468 cal / 29g protein per serving over 8 servings for the pork alone, which is already dinner-weight before rice. Slow-braised, shreds, holds for a week. The live catalog's New Mexican entry is green chili; adovada is the red-chile counterpart and a different dish.

candidates.name: Chipotle Sweet Potato Pork Chili
candidates.why: Every signature ingredient maps to a tracked commodity (chipotle-adobo, poblano-peppers, sweet-potatoes, both bean ids). Source verified at 349 cal / 40g protein per serving over 10 servings; add cornbread or rice and it is a 500+ cal dinner with an excellent protein-to-calorie ratio. Catalog has beef and turkey chilis but no pork chili.

candidates.name: Morisqueta (Michoacan Pork, Rice and Beans)
unmapped_flags: queso fresco garnish (shredded-cheese or feta substitutes)
candidates.why: Verified on the source at 573 cal / 31g protein per serving over 6 servings, which is exactly the profile we want with no adjustment. Built as layered rice + beans + saucy pork, so it is already a weigh-and-divide bowl. Source uses pork ribs; swapping to board-tracked pork-shoulder keeps it cheap. No morisqueta in the catalog.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Pork Birria Bowls
candidates.why: Source verified at 422 cal / 39g protein per serving over 6 servings, and the consomme-braised pork holds beautifully for meal prep. Chipotle-adobo version means no whole dried chiles needed, so every ingredient maps to the board. Beef birria/barbacoa is a separate slice (B2); no pork birria exists in the catalog.

candidates.name: Pork Enchilada Verde Casserole
candidates.why: Layered like a lasagna rather than rolled, so it scales to a 14-serving hotel pan and cuts into even portions. Confidence note: source publishes no nutrition panel; est_cal estimated from tortillas + cheese + pork ratios. Dedup flag: the catalog already has Slow Cooker Salsa Verde Pork Bowls - same sauce family, different dish format (baked casserole with tortillas and cheese). Worth an explicit dedup ruling.

candidates.name: Pork and Calabacitas Stew in Chipotle Tomato Sauce
candidates.why: Uses zucchini as a cheap volume vegetable, which keeps the cost per serving down while the pork shoulder carries protein. Confidence note: source lists no nutrition, so est_cal is my estimate served over rice. Distinct from every live pork entry (no chile-verde, no BBQ, no Asian glaze) and a good template for cheap summer squash weeks.

candidates.name: Sudado de Cerdo (Colombian Pork and Potato Stew)
unmapped_flags: yuca (optional; drop it and use more potato)
sazon con azafran (paprika + turmeric + bouillon substitute, all board-tracked)
candidates.why: One-pot braise served over white rice; potatoes and rice carry calories and the pork chops carry protein. Confidence note: source has no nutrition panel and yields only 4 servings, so est_cal is my estimate scaled to our portion. Colombian cuisine is entirely absent from the catalog.

candidates.name: Frijol con Puerco (Yucatecan Pork and Black Beans)
unmapped_flags: epazote (optional herb; cilantro substitutes and is board-tracked)
candidates.why: Beans-and-pork one pot that is genuinely cheap per serving: black beans do the calorie work and pork shoulder does the protein work. Confidence note: source publishes no nutrition data, so est_cal is estimated. Different dish from feijoada (Yucatecan, tomato-radish-lime service, no bacon/sausage), but the dedup stage should confirm they both earn slots.

candidates.name: Mexican Chipotle Pork and Beans
unmapped_flags: butter/lima beans in the original (swap to board-tracked canned-pinto-beans or canned-white-beans)
candidates.why: Source verified at 323 cal / 27g protein per serving over 8 servings for the braise; over rice it is a 520-560 cal dinner. Braised 3 hours, shreds, reheats well. Dedup note: overlaps thematically with frijol con puerco above - if only one pork-and-beans dish survives, this is the more approachable American-pantry version.

candidates.name: Arroz con Gandules with Pork
unmapped_flags: gandules / pigeon peas (no board id - closest tracked substitutes are canned-pinto-beans or chickpeas)
sofrito (build from board-tracked onions, bell-peppers, garlic, cilantro)
candidates.why: Puerto Rico's signature rice dish, made a real dinner by cooking pork shoulder chunks into it. Source verified at 429 cal / 13g protein per serving - too low as written, so our version must roughly double the pork to hit 25g+. Confidence note: est_cal reflects that heavier-pork rebuild, not the source's ratio. Flagged because the signature ingredient (gandules) has no board home.

candidates.name: Ecuadorian Hornado (Slow Roasted Pork) Bowls
unmapped_flags: beer or chicha marinade (no board id; the recipe works with broth or apple-juice)
candidates.why: Slow-roasted achiote-garlic pork shoulder, served with rice and potatoes. Confidence note: source lists 10 servings but no nutrition panel, so est_cal is my estimate. Ecuadorian cuisine is completely absent from the catalog and achiote-paste is board-tracked, so the flavor base is already priced.

candidates.name: Achiote Pork Chops with Rice and Beans
candidates.why: Simple achiote-citrus marinade on board-tracked pork-chops. Confidence note: source is a 2-serving pan-sear with no nutrition data; our version would be a sheet-pan roast of marinated chops so it scales to 14, and est_cal is my estimate for chop + rice + beans. Batch-scalable as written only if we move it to the oven, which is the intended adaptation.

candidates.name: Peruvian-Style Pork Lomo Saltado Bowls
unmapped_flags: aji amarillo (optional; chili-powder or hot-sauce substitutes)
candidates.why: Rice plus oven-baked fries plus seared pork strips is a genuinely 600+ cal bowl and Peruvian cuisine is missing from the catalog. Confidence note: no nutrition panel on source, and this is the riskiest batch candidate in the slice - a stir-fry by nature. It scales only as a sheet-pan roast of pork strips and vegetables with the fries baked separately; flag for the writer to adapt, or drop if the auditor calls it fried-to-order.

candidates.name: Pulled Pork Enchilada Bake
candidates.why: Source verified at 772 cal / 39g protein per serving over 4 servings, so trimming cheese slightly still leaves a 650-700 cal dinner with strong protein. Every ingredient is a tracked commodity. Assembled as a pan bake it divides cleanly at 14 servings. Catalog has chicken and beef enchilada dishes but no pork.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Pork and Sauerkraut with Apples and Potatoes
candidates.why: Sauerkraut, apples and apple-juice are all board commodities, making this one of the cheapest pork dinners in the slice. Source verified at 267 cal / 38g protein per serving over 8 servings for the pork and kraut; add mashed or roasted potatoes and it lands 500-550 cal with an outstanding protein ratio. New Year's Day Midwest staple, nothing like it in the catalog.

candidates.name: Farmhouse Pork Chop and Stuffing Casserole
candidates.why: Source verified at 957 cal / 73g protein per serving over 8 servings, which is above our target - we would cut butter and soup to land near 700 cal while keeping 40g+ protein. Pure pantry-commodity casserole (stuffing-mix and cream-of-chicken-soup are both tracked), bakes in one pan, portions by weight. Catalog has no stuffing-based dish at all.

candidates.name: Pulled Pork Baked Mac and Cheese
candidates.why: Verified at 547 cal / 28g protein per serving over 12 servings straight from the source - already sitting in our target window. Baked in a 9x13, divides by weight. Distinct from the live BBQ Pulled Pork Rice Bowl (pasta bake with cheese sauce, not a rice bowl), though the dedup stage should confirm the pulled-pork base does not read as a repeat.

candidates.name: Pulled Pork Tamale Pie with Cornbread Topping
candidates.why: Source verified at 412 cal / 25g protein per serving over 9 servings; bumping the pork slightly puts it at 500+ cal and 28g+. Corn-muffin-mix is board-tracked so the topping is cheap. The catalog's cornbread dish is beef Chili Cornbread Casserole - this is a pork shredded-meat version with green chiles, a different build.

candidates.name: Dutch Oven Pork Loin Roast with Potatoes and Gravy
unmapped_flags: fresh thyme and rosemary (board tracks dried-thyme; dried works)
apple cider (apple-juice is the tracked stand-in)
candidates.why: Verified at 621 cal / 72g protein per serving over 6 servings - the best protein-to-calorie ratio in this slice. Roast, vegetables and gravy all cook in one pot, which is exactly how a 14-serving batch should run. Nothing like a straight pork roast dinner exists in the catalog.

candidates.name: Sheet Pan Pork Tenderloin with Potatoes and Green Beans
candidates.why: Verified at 400 cal / 40g protein per serving over 5 servings; adding a bit more potato brings it to 500+ with 40g protein intact. Every ingredient is board-tracked and pork-tenderloin is a tracked commodity. Sheet-pan format is the cleanest batch method we have. The live Grilled Pork Tenderloin Burrito Bowl is a completely different dish.

candidates.name: Cowboy Pork and Beans Biscuit Bake
candidates.why: Verified at 527 cal / 25g protein per serving over 5 servings - right on target with no adjustment. Uses ground-pork, bacon, baked-beans and refrigerated-biscuits, all tracked commodities, which makes it one of the cheapest builds in the slice. No ground-pork American casserole in the catalog (the two live ground-pork dishes are Korean and Asian meatball).

candidates.name: No-Peek Pork Chop and Rice Casserole
candidates.why: Source verified at 415 cal / 26g protein per serving over 4 servings; scaling the chop weight up gets us past 500 cal at 30g+. Five pantry ingredients, all board-tracked (onion-soup-mix and cream-of-mushroom-soup included), dump-and-bake, and the rice cooks in the dish. Distinct from the live Southern Smothered Pork Chops and Rice (baked casserole, not stovetop gravy).

candidates.name: BBQ Pulled Pork Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
unmapped_flags: liquid smoke (optional; paprika or bbq-sauce covers it)
candidates.why: Verified at 432 cal / 36g protein per serving over 4 servings; a slightly larger sweet potato puts it over 500. Sweet-potatoes are board-tracked and cheap, and the meal preps well as pork-in-one-container, potato-in-another. Different vehicle from the live BBQ Pulled Pork Rice Bowl - dedup should confirm the sweet potato base makes it its own dish.

candidates.name: Pulled Pork Shepherd's Pie
unmapped_flags: red wine (optional; beef-broth substitutes and is tracked)
candidates.why: Verified at 661 cal / 50g protein per serving over 8 servings - dinner-sized with excellent protein. Mashed-potato-topped bake portions perfectly by weight and reheats better than most. No shepherd's pie of any protein in the catalog.

candidates.name: Pork Chops and Scalloped Potatoes Casserole
candidates.why: Source verified at 399 cal / 37g protein per serving over 6 servings; adding cheese and a slightly heavier potato layer brings it to 500+ with protein intact. Six cheap tracked ingredients. Distinct from the live Cheesy Pork Chop and Hash Brown Casserole (sliced fresh potatoes in cream sauce rather than frozen hash browns) - worth a dedup ruling.

candidates.name: Country Pork Meatballs with Onion Gravy over Mashed Potatoes
unmapped_flags: fresh sage (no board id; the flavor is central - dried sage is a cheap pantry add but is not currently tracked)
candidates.why: Source verified at 548 cal / 28g protein per serving over 4 servings before mashed potatoes, so plated it is a 640 cal dinner. Ground-pork is board-tracked and among the cheapest proteins we buy. Bake the meatballs on sheet pans and the gravy in one pot and it scales to 14 easily. The catalog's only pork meatball is Thai-style.

candidates.name: Oven Baked Country-Style Pork Chops with Potatoes
candidates.why: Verified at 555 cal / 27g protein per serving over 4 servings, exactly the target, and every single ingredient is a board commodity. One sheet pan, chops and potatoes together, no browning step - a clean 14-serving batch. The pantry-sauce glaze makes it different from every live pork chop entry (all of which are gravy- or breading-based).

candidates.name: Slow Cooker BBQ Country Style Pork Ribs over Rice
unmapped_flags: country-style pork ribs (board tracks baby-back-ribs and pork-shoulder, not country-style ribs - they are cut from the shoulder, so pork-shoulder is the price proxy)
candidates.why: Verified at 576 cal / 44g protein per serving over 4 servings for the meat alone; over rice it is a 640 cal dinner with a very strong protein ratio. Five-minute prep slow cooker dish. The live Brazilian-Style Pork Ribs Bowls are a different cut and flavor profile, but flag for the dedup stage since both are rib-and-rice bowls.

candidates.name: Dump-and-Bake Pork Chops with Apples and Stuffing
candidates.why: Verified at 539 cal / 26g protein per serving over 4 servings with no adjustment needed. All-commodity ingredient list, zero prep beyond slicing, one pan. Dedup note: shares stuffing-mix with the Farmhouse casserole above and apples with the sauerkraut dish - the fruit-and-savory glaze build is distinct from both, but the dedup stage should decide whether all three earn slots.

candidates.name: Creamy Pork Stew with Potatoes and Carrots
unmapped_flags: fresh rosemary and sage (dried-thyme and italian-seasoning are the tracked substitutes)
candidates.why: Verified at 567 cal / 41g protein per serving over 6 servings - target profile with no adjustment. The source author explicitly bought 2.5 lbs of pork butt for $2.47, which is exactly the budget story the site tells. Stovetop or slow cooker, both scale. Different from the Dutch oven roast above (cubed stew in a cream broth, not a sliced roast).

candidates.name: Slow-Roasted Pork Shoulder with Onion Gravy
unmapped_flags: white wine (chicken-broth substitutes and is tracked)
fennel seeds (not tracked; optional)
candidates.why: Source states roughly 746 cal per serving over 10-12 servings, so we would trim the fat cap and plate with potatoes to land near 700 with 45g+ protein. Cheapest pork cut on the board, one pan, three hours unattended. Dedup note: with the Dutch oven loin roast and the crock pot vegetable roast both in the pool, at most two straight pork roasts should survive.

candidates.name: Glazed Pork Sirloin Roast with Roasted Vegetables
unmapped_flags: pork sirloin roast (board tracks pork-tenderloin, pork-chops and pork-shoulder; sirloin roast has no id - pork-shoulder or a loin roast is the price proxy)
orange marmalade (jelly is the closest tracked commodity)
candidates.why: Verified at 329 cal / 52g protein per serving over 6 servings for the meat, one of the leanest high-protein cuts available; add roasted potatoes and carrots for a 540 cal dinner. Sear-and-roast method scales to two sheet pans at 14 servings. Flagged because the specific cut is not priced on the board.

candidates.name: Fritada de Chancho (Ecuadorian Braised Pork) Bowls
unmapped_flags: plantains and mote/hominy sides (hominy is tracked; plantains are not)
candidates.why: Pork simmered in citrus and water until the liquid cooks off and the meat browns in its own fat - one pot, no added oil, and it uses the cheapest cut. Confidence note: source gives neither servings nor nutrition, so est_cal is my estimate served over rice and beans. Second Ecuadorian entry alongside hornado; if only one survives dedup, hornado is the more distinctive roast.

candidates.name: Colombian Pork Loin with Blackberry Sauce
unmapped_flags: white wine (chicken-broth or apple-juice substitutes, both tracked)
candidates.why: Roast pork loin with a tart blackberry pan sauce; blackberries are a tracked board commodity so this becomes a genuinely cheap dish in berry season and a signal to members that the board drives the menu. Confidence note: source has no nutrition panel and serves 4, so est_cal is my estimate for loin plus rice. Nothing fruit-sauced exists in the catalog.
